text:
alana: heads-up  did a quick walkthrough of deep-links across Console routes. Noticed a couple of small but annoying UX edgecases around sidebar reveal + breadcrumbs when fallback routing kicks in.

mike: quick summary?

alana: repro notes: open a deep link to Project > Models > MyModel > Revisions -> opens fine, main content focused, but left rail stays collapsed to the top-level group and breadcrumb shows "Models > ..." rather than the full path. Keyboard users tab and lose context.

sara: is this only when we route via fallback (i.e., route normalization)? Or any deep-link?

alana: mostly when the route matcher falls back to a compatible route (we hit canonicalization code). Also happens when the app does a redirect to a model alias name.

tom: proposed fixes: 1) ensure we sync rail expansion with router restore, 2) set aria-current on the revealed item and programmatically move focus to the rail entry (but avoid scrolling main content unexpectedly), 3) update breadcrumb state after router fallback completes.

jess: UX note: when we auto-expand a lot of rail nodes it can feel like the nav is jumping. Suggest an interim micro animation + reduced-motion respect. Also consider a minimal "reveal" affordance so we don't blow up the entire rail every deep-link.

sara: accessibility: when focusing the rail item always ensure keyboard focus ring is visible (not just color change) and that the element is reachable by Tab. Use role="link" and aria-current="page", and add an aria-live announcement like "Navigation: Models older expanded" for screen readers.

mike: implementation detail: router emits a post-redirect event (router:restored). We can subscribe and run a small reconcile routine: find rail node by data-path, expand ancestors, set aria-current, but call focus with preventScroll:true and then container.scrollIntoView({block:'nearest'}) if the item is outside the rail viewport.

tom: also check mobile: we have a collapsed drawer variant. If deep-link lands in drawer mode, reveal the drawer and highlight the item. For touch targets bump cluster header tappable area to 48px min.

jess: copy tweak: breadcrumb truncation currently uses "..." which hides context. Can we instead show the last two segments and keep a collapsed affordance for earlier path? e.g., "Org / Models / MyModel" -> show "Org / ... / MyModel" and expose full on hover or screen reader.

sara: that helps. Also make sure breadcrumb separators are accessible (not purely visual).

devops-bot: Canary deploy of rail-reveal fix queued for next nightly build.

mike: test plan: unit tests for aria-current toggling, e2e deep-link scenario on desktop + mobile, and an accessibility snapshot to assert live region contains expected phrase.

jess: style tokens: will add token for focus outline thickness + contrast, and adjust spacing token for cluster header hit area.

alana: experiment idea: 5% of sessions show an ephemeral toast on deep-link: "Show in left nav" with "Reveal" button. Track clicks and subsequent nav to see if users want explicit reveal. If low click-thru, we default to silent expansion.

sara: open question: if we always expand on deep-link, could that break users who intentionally collapsed sections? Might need a user-level preference or preserve prior user-state where applicable.

tom: agree. Prefer: local session preference wins unless user explicitly followed a deep-link from an external source (detect via `navigation.state && navigation.type === 'navigate'` or referrer header).

mike: will add an integration test to ensure previous collapse state persists across route-only navigations but is overridden on external deep-link.

jess: I'll prototype micro animation in Figma and push a frame.

alana: summary / action items: 1) eng to implement router restore hook + rail reconcile (mike), 2) a11y tasks (sara) - live region + focus ring + reduced-motion, 3) design (jess) - animation + breadcrumb truncation copy, 4) product to sign-off experiment (alana). I'll create a PR and link issue #4399. If no objections I'll tag eng-runtime and schedule the canary. :thumbsup:
